status: draft — first indexing pass 2026-08-06, roster confirmed with user before full build (learned from the Genesis round-trip)
notes: Same schema and rules as Genesis.json. Submanagers attach to whichever major figure they actually relate to in the text, not defaulted to Moses just because he's central — corrected by the user 2026-08-06. 'role: named' entries are genealogy/context only, no gameplay perk. A person named only in a LATER book of the Bible is still given their later name here when scripture ITSELF explicitly links the two mentions (e.g. Jannes/Jambres in 2 Timothy 3:8, which explicitly says they withstood Moses) — but NOT when a name is merely traditionally associated without the text explicitly making the connection (e.g. Pharaoh's daughter is NOT set to 'Bithiah' here — see her entry for why).

characters.name: Moses

verses.note: Birth; hidden three months, then set adrift and drawn from the water
The burning bush
Confronts Pharaoh through the ten plagues
Parts the Red Sea
Receives the Ten Commandments
His face shines after speaking with God

funFacts: Raised in Pharaoh's household but nursed as an infant by his own mother, who was hired as his nurse without Pharaoh's household knowing the relation (Exodus 2:7-9).

characters.name: Aaron

verses.note: Appointed as Moses' spokesman
His rod becomes a serpent before Pharaoh
Helps Hur hold up Moses' hands at the battle with Amalek
Consecrated as the first high priest
Builds the golden calf under pressure from the people

funFacts: Three years older than Moses (Exodus 7:7), and the one who does the actual speaking to Pharaoh in the early chapters, per Exodus 4:16.

characters.name: Zipporah

verses.note: Moses meets her and her sisters at a well in Midian
Circumcises her son with 'a sharp stone' to turn away the LORD's anger from Moses — one of the strangest passages in the book
Jethro brings her and her sons to Moses in the wilderness

funFacts: Not to be confused with Asenath, Joseph's Egyptian wife back in Genesis (41:45) — two different women married to two different major figures, a full book apart.

characters.name: Pharaoh (of the Exodus)

verses.note: 'A new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph' — begins the oppression
Refuses Moses and Aaron's first request
Repeatedly hardens his heart through the plagues
Pursues Israel to the Red Sea; his army destroyed

funFacts: Never given a personal name anywhere in scripture — unlike later Pharaohs such as Pharaoh Necho or Pharaoh Shishak in Kings/Chronicles, who are named. A different, also-unnamed man from Joseph's Pharaoh in Genesis 41.

characters.name: Miriam

verses.note: Watches the basket in the reeds and arranges for Jochebed to nurse Moses (unnamed in this scene, but understood to be her)
Called 'the prophetess' — leads the women in song and dance after the Red Sea

funFacts: First person in the Bible explicitly called a prophetess (Exodus 15:20).

characters.name: Joshua

verses.note: First appearance in scripture — leads Israel's fighting men against Amalek while Moses' raised hands (held up by Aaron and Hur) hold the battle
Attends Moses partway up Mount Sinai
Moses' minister; does not leave the tabernacle

funFacts: Called 'Oshea the son of Nun' when first commanding this battle — his father Nun and the fuller family background come later (Numbers 13:8, 13:16).

characters.name: Hur

verses.note: With Aaron, physically holds up Moses' hands on a stone seat through the entire battle with Amalek — when the hands dropped, Israel began losing
Left in charge of the people with Aaron while Moses is on Sinai

funFacts: Promoted to a full manager rather than a submanager specifically because the text makes his physical support the deciding factor in the battle's outcome (Exodus 17:11-12) — without him and Aaron, Moses could not sustain the position alone.

characters.name: Jethro

verses.note: Priest of Midian, gives Zipporah to Moses in marriage
Brings Moses' wife and sons to him and offers sacrifice
Advises Moses to delegate judgment to appointed leaders — the origin of Israel's tiered judicial structure

funFacts: Also called Reuel earlier in the same book (Exodus 2:18) — most likely one man known by two names/titles, not two different people; flagged here rather than silently picking one.

characters.name: Bezaleel

verses.note: 'Filled... with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship' — chief craftsman of the tabernacle
Named again as construction begins, paired with Aholiab
Builds the ark, the altar, and the tabernacle's furnishings

funFacts: Of the tribe of Judah — the first person in the Bible explicitly said to be filled with the Spirit of God for a specific task, and that task is skilled craftsmanship, not prophecy or leadership.

characters.name: Aholiab

verses.note: Given by name alongside Bezaleel to help build the tabernacle
Specifically skilled as 'an engraver, and a cunning workman, and an embroiderer'

funFacts: Of the tribe of Dan — paired with Bezaleel (tribe of Judah) as co-lead craftsmen, spanning two different tribes for the one shared project.

verses.note: Named as Moses and Aaron's father, of the tribe of Levi
Hides Moses three months, then nurses him for Pharaoh's own daughter, unnamed in this scene but understood to be her
Named
Named — 'I have been a stranger in a strange land'

characters.name: Eliezer (Moses' son)
characters.perkNote: Accuracy flag: a DIFFERENT man from Eliezer of Damascus, Abraham's steward in Genesis 15:2 — same KJV spelling, unrelated, a full book apart.

verses.note: Named — 'the God of my father... delivered me from the sword of Pharaoh'
Goes up part of Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Abihu, and seventy elders
Named among those consecrated as priests with Aaron
Goes up part of Mount Sinai with Moses, Aaron, Nadab, and seventy elders
Named among those consecrated as priests with Aaron

characters.name: Shiphrah
characters.perkNote: She defies Pharaoh rather than serving him — attached to his tier as the one who directly opposed him, not as a loyal supporter.

verses.note: One of two named Hebrew midwives who defy Pharaoh's order to kill Hebrew baby boys; God deals well with her for it

characters.name: Puah
characters.perkNote: Same note as Shiphrah — defies Pharaoh rather than serving him.

verses.note: The second of the two named Hebrew midwives who defy Pharaoh

characters.name: Jannes
characters.perkNote: Never named in Exodus itself — only 'the magicians of Egypt' (Exodus 7:11, 7:22, 8:7, 8:18-19, 9:11). Named here because 2 Timothy 3:8 explicitly identifies Jannes and Jambres as the ones who 'withstood Moses,' making the cross-reference textually explicit rather than merely traditional.

verses.note: Unnamed as 'the magicians' — replicate some of Moses' signs, then fail
New Testament — names Jannes and Jambres directly as the ones who withstood Moses

characters.name: Jambres
characters.perkNote: Same note as Jannes — unnamed in Exodus, named via the explicit 2 Timothy 3:8 cross-reference.

verses.note: Unnamed as 'the magicians'
New Testament — names Jannes and Jambres directly
Named as Aaron's wife, sister of Naashon

characters.name: Eleazar

verses.note: Named among Aaron's four sons

funFacts: Not yet prominent in Exodus itself — becomes far more significant in Numbers and Joshua, after Nadab and Abihu die (Leviticus 10).

verses.note: Named among Aaron's four sons

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

jethroOtherDaughters.note: 'The priest of Midian had seven daughters' — only Zipporah is named; the other six are not.

pharaohsDaughter.note: Never named in Exodus. NOT set to 'Bithiah' here — 1 Chronicles 4:18 names a 'Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh' in an unrelated genealogical fragment, with no explicit textual link to the woman who drew Moses from the water. That identification is a later Jewish tradition, not something the Bible itself states — kept unnamed here rather than asserting an inference as fact.
